$comment: The DU (dual) rows of spec 00024 §6.B (project 00024-03): which rows of deployments/reference-set.json this repository generates as DUAL contracts — the FULL MIP-0018 metadata of the row's MIP-18 twin (acedward/mip-0018-midnight-contracts, the `18` variant: every declaration step for step, long values as ONE circuit call emitting all their parts in one intent) AND a public interface. scripts/generate-du-contracts.ts reads it (with reference-set.json) and writes contracts/generated/<ID>.compact and deployments/dual-matrix.json. Every DU contract: the emitter secret (the constructor stores its hash; every emitting circuit — each MIP-0018 declaration and `publishBundle` — checks it, spec Q12), a `repository` declaration (the URL of its own source on `main`), `publishBundle(payload)` behind the secret, and the token itself on OpenZeppelin Compact Contracts v0.4.0-alpha.3 where a module exists (vendored, contracts/vendor/openzeppelin/), otherwise this repository's own native unshielded template. Its interface is HIDDEN (the Public Interfaces draft's private form): a separate interface source declares the deployed ledger slots in order under hidden names, imports no module, and publishes the code of every IMPURE circuit (spec Q9) — each DU contract also exports one PURE constant getter, which the interface does not publish (a pure circuit has no verifier key). Bundle URLs are `bundleBase` + `bundlePath` + `index.json` (the local stack's static server as the compose network names it); a bundle's bytes depend on its URL, so the URL is fixed here, not at deploy time.

rows.covers: a ~700-byte `metadata` JSON value (one declaration in 3 parts) beside a HIDDEN interface verified L1/L2/L3 (OpenZeppelin NativeShieldedToken)
a rename, a Null that clears `description`, then a ~400-byte `description` in 2 parts (positioned by its first part, P1), beside a HIDDEN interface (OpenZeppelin FungibleToken)
mints before its metadata (observed, then described); a native unshielded token (own template: OpenZeppelin has no native unshielded module)
two tokens in one contract — one domain separator, kind 0 and kind 1, one colour — and one HIDDEN interface (OpenZeppelin NativeShieldedToken for the shielded half, own code for the unshielded half)
